hints: Focus on how the side chain is joined to the main carbon backbone, not just the atoms in it.
Notice each substituted backbone carbon is bonded to O, which is then bonded to C=O and CH3, giving a -O-C(=O)-CH3 group.
Take one two-carbon repeat of -CH2-CH(side group)- and restore the C=C double bond to rebuild the original alkene monomer.
walkthrough:
**Identify the addition polymer backbone**

Remember an addition polymer has a long C-C single bond backbone. Each original alkene C=C becomes a C-C unit in the chain.

So look for a repeating -CH2-CHX- pattern.

**Identify the side group X**

Look closely at the branches. Each branch carbon is attached via O to a $\text{C=O}$ which is attached to $\text{CH}_3$.

That group is:
$$-\text{O}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_3$$
This is an ethanoate ester linked through oxygen, often called an acetoxy group.

**Rebuild the monomer**

Take one repeat unit:
$$-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OCOCH}_3)-$$
Reverse polymerisation by putting a double bond back between the two backbone carbons:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{O}-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_3$$
This is ethenyl ethanoate, also called vinyl acetate, which matches option A.

options.A: Correct. This is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}=\text{CH}_2$, ethenyl ethanoate. Its C=C opens to give $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OCOCH}_3)-$ repeats. The backbone attaches to O, O attaches to C=O, C=O attaches to CH3, exactly as seen in the polymer section.
options.B: Wrong. This is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCO}_2\text{CH}_3$, methyl propenoate. Its polymer would have $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{OCH}_3)-$. Here the backbone attaches directly to C=O, not to O. That is the reverse ester connectivity to the polymer shown.
options.C: Wrong. This is a diketone alkene, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}=\text{CHCOCH}_3$. It has ketone $\text{C=O}$ groups and no ester O linkage, and it has 6 carbons with an internal C=C. It could not give pendant $-\text{OCOCH}_3$ groups.
options.D: Wrong. This is $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{OCOCH}_3)_2$, with two ethanoate groups on the same alkene carbon. Its polymer would give $-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{OCOCH}_3)_2-$, i.e. two side groups on one backbone carbon and none on the neighbour. The polymer shown has only one side group per substituted carbon.
